solution:
With $u=1+x^{2}$ we have $du=2x\,dx$, so $x\,dx=\tfrac12du$.
When $x=0$, $u=1$; when $x=1$, $u=2$. Hence
$$\int_{0}^{1}\frac{x}{\sqrt{1+x^{2}}}\,dx=\int_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{\sqrt{u}}\cdot\tfrac12\,du=\tfrac12\bigl[2\sqrt{u}\bigr]_{1}^{2}=\sqrt{2}-1.$$
(Check: an antiderivative is $\sqrt{1+x^{2}}$, giving $\sqrt2-1$.)
hints: Note that x dx is half of du.
Change the limits to u = 1 and u = 2.
